rules: Layout: icon at the inline start, then a column with title and description, then action and dismiss at the inline end, all aligned with the first line. padding surrounds everything; iconGap separates the icon, the column, the action and dismiss; titleGap separates title from description.
title is required plain text in typographyTitle and content; description is optional plain text in typography and descriptionColor. Both wrap; the toast grows in block size.

intent sets the intrinsic glyph (neutral and info: info, success: check-circle, warning: warning, danger: warning-circle) at iconSize in iconColor, hidden from assistive technology; the icon part may replace it. The surface stays neutral: the words carry the message, the icon only reinforces it.
The container is painted in surface with shadow, an edge of borderWidth in elevationColor and radius corners; its inline size is inlineSize, or the available inline size of the region when smaller.

action holds at most one small (sm) Button, neutral and outline by default, for an immediate follow-up (Undo, View). The same action stays available elsewhere in the interface: a toast is never the only way to reach it.
dismiss is always present: a small ghost neutral IconButton with the intrinsic close glyph and dismissLabel as its accessible name.

A toast with duration greater than 0 and no action dismisses itself duration milliseconds after it appears. The countdown is paused while the pointer is over the region, while focus is inside the region and while the document is hidden; it resumes with the time that was left. A toast with an action or with duration 0 stays until it is dismissed or its action is activated.

The toast emits dismiss when its dismiss button is activated, when its countdown ends, when Escape is pressed while focus is inside it, and after its action is activated; the application removes it from the region.

A toast enters from the region's edge, moving enterDistance towards its place and fading in over motionDuration with easingEnter, and leaves by fading out over motionDuration with easingExit while the others close the gap; under reduced motion it only fades.

dismiss.when: A toast asks to leave the region: its dismiss button, the end of its countdown, Escape inside it, or the activation of its action.
dismiss.payload: The toast that asks to leave.

rules: A toast is a brief notification about something the user just did or that just happened in the background (Saved, Message sent, Upload failed); it appears above the page, does not block it and leaves by itself unless it holds an action. A durable message is an Alert; a message that must be answered is a Dialog.

The region is a single landmark per page, named by label, that holds the toasts in the order the application provides them. It stays above the page and above open dialogs, outside the flow, at edge from the viewport edges named by placement (top or bottom, start, center or end), and stacks its toasts separated by gap: the newest toast is nearest the edge named by placement.
At most max toasts are shown; further toasts wait and appear, in order, as shown toasts leave.
The application owns the list of toasts: it adds a toast to show it and removes it when the toast emits dismiss.

Toasts are announced when they appear, politely for every intent except danger, which is announced assertively; appearing never moves focus. The region is reachable by keyboard in its reading order: each action and dismiss button is a stop in sequential focus.
Where the platform has no top layer, the region is stacked at layer.
In forced-colors mode each toast keeps a visible edge in the system text color.
